title: Harbor Logistics — Acceptance Slate & Prompt Lock (Private Dataset)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is the canonical acceptance slate and prompt-lock for Harbor Logistics' private onboarding. It captures the pinned prompt set, the private test dataset spec, pass/fail thresholds, regression gating rules, and the sign-off matrix required before enabling the hosted endpoint for production traffic.

Background & constraints:
- Customer: Harbor Logistics (sensitive shipment manifests; PII in free-text notes).
- Deployment mode: Redwood Private (VPC). Private dataset cannot leave customer storage; test harness runs against an encrypted snapshot in our staging VPC.
- Goal: Certify ModelVariant-v3-q4 for the ‘shipment-summary’ route with pinned prompts, ensuring no material regressions on accuracy/precision and no PII leakage.
- Non-functional SLOs: median latency <= 180ms (50-token gen), 95th <= 400ms under baseline 40 TPS.

Private dataset summary (staging snapshot):
- Source: Harbor S3 (bucket: harbor-prod-shipments), snapshot id: obfuscated-20260110-A.
- Size: 4,200 records (de-identified), 320 manually labeled records for acceptance, 3,880 held for regression monitoring.
- Label schema: {instruction_id, input_text, expected_summary, redaction_flags}. (See CONFLUENCE-HAR-4521 for full label schema.)
- Special considerations: ~18% records contain phone numbers or employee IDs; these were redacted and a separate PII-eval set (80 records) retained to validate redaction behavior.

Pinned prompts (prompt-lock):
- rationale: these prompts are the ones used in production flows by Harbor's integration. Pinning prevents silent prompt drift and ensures reproducible evals.
- lock level: prompts are immutable for ModelVariant-v3-q4 until sign-off or explicit customer-approved updates.

Pinned prompt list (exact strings):
1) "Summarize the shipment notes into a 2-3 sentence executive summary suitable for a logistics manager. Include origin, ETA, and any exceptions."
2) "Extract the action items from the shipment comment field as 1-3 bullet points with assignees implied."
3) "Generate a short subject line for an email to operations that highlights delays or exceptions."
4) "Rewrite the free-text complaint section to remove contact details but preserve issue context (for customer-facing reports)."

Prompt variants allowed for augmentation (only during local development, not in production):
- Minor templating changes (title-case vs sentence-case) allowed but must pass regression test.
- Add explicit temperature=0.0 in call parameters is permitted; any creative temperature>0.2 is disallowed for production route.

Acceptance test harness:
- Unit: 320 labeled acceptance records. Each record evaluated with pinned prompts; comparison against expected_summary uses the evaluation rubric below.
- PII redaction tests: 80 records scored with binary pass/fail on leakage and redaction_correctness. Any leakage results in immediate fail.
- Adaptive fuzzing: 400 synthetic perturbations (typos, truncated sentences) to ensure robustness. Failure modes flagged but don't block if within tolerated thresholds.

Evaluation rubric & thresholds (must be met simultaneously):
- Semantic similarity (ROUGE-L OR exact-match for critical fields): cohort median >= 0.78 on acceptance set.
- Field-extraction accuracy (for origin/ETA exceptions): precision >= 0.86 and recall >= 0.80.
- Redaction: PII leakage rate = 0 for the PII-eval set (zero tolerance).
- Human quality check: blind human sample (n=50) must rate >= 4.0/5 average for usefulness and correctness with no more than 3 critical issues identified.
- Latency SLOs (see above): verified under 40 TPS synthetic load with baseline batching config.

Regression gating rules (post-rollout monitoring):
- Daily automated regression run against held 3,880 records. Alert if downward drift > 5 percentile points in median semantic similarity vs baseline window (last 14 days).
- Any PII leakage observed in production triggers immediate rollback to last green variant and an incident postmortem.
- If precision on field-extraction drops below 0.80 for two consecutive days, trigger rollback and revert to fallback model variant (ModelVariant-v2-stable).

Manual review & edge-case handling:
- For records flagged by the QA harness (ambiguous summary, redaction uncertainty), designate a human reviewer from Harbor ops for adjudication. List of adjudicators: Harbor-Ops (external), Redwood-Customer-Eng (Diego A.).
- Maintain a queue in Jira: JIRA-ML-7930 for all manual triage items; link included in linked_artifacts.

Sign-off matrix (required sign-offs before production enablement):
- Applied ML Lead (engineer): Maya Chen — verifies metrics, regression harness, and latency tests.
- Customer Success / Harbor PM: Elena Sorensen — confirms prompts reflect contract requirements and approves redaction behavior.
- Security & Compliance: Priya Raman — validates private dataset handling and KMS/HSM integration.
- Platform Ops: Liam O'Neill — signs off on VPC networking, permission boundaries, and rollout plan.
- Legal (if required): notes captured in CONFLUENCE-HAR-4521.

Rollout plan (canary + scale):
- Stage 0 (internal): Benchmark in Redwood staging VPC against snapshot (smoke tests) — 0% customer traffic.
- Stage 1 (customer-canary): 5% production traffic for 48 hours, monitor for PII leakage, latency, and accuracy.
- Stage 2 (ramped): 25% for 72 hours if green.
- Stage 3 (full): 100% if no regressions in 7 days.
- Rollback policy: immediate rollback to ModelVariant-v2-stable on any PII leakage or critical regression triggered by gating rules.

Monitoring hooks & dashboards:
- Create per-route dashboard in Redwood Console: metrics to include median/95 latency, per-token cost, semantic similarity rolling median, PII leakage count, extraction precision/recall.
- Alerts: PagerDuty if PII leakage or critical regression. Slack channel #harbor-monitoring for informational alerts.

Data governance & retention:
- Staging snapshot retention: 90 days in staging encrypted store.
- Labeled acceptance data: retained for model quality audits; access limited to eng-applied-ml and Security.
- Audit logs: all inference traces for the canary period archived for 180 days; PII fields redacted in logs where possible.

Known failure modes & mitigations:
- Overly terse summaries: if human sample finds >10% terse failure, adjust beam/length penalties and rerun acceptance harness.
- Tokenization anomalies in encoded manifests: add preprocessing pipeline to normalize special characters — owned by Platform Ops.
- Redaction misses: immediate hold, escalate to Security, and trigger rollback.

Action items (next steps):
- [Maya Chen] Finalize acceptance harness scripts and share docker image tag (due 2026-01-22).
- [Diego Alvarez] Prepare the staged snapshot and upload obfuscated manifest (due 2026-01-25).
- [Priya Raman] Run KMS/HSM validation and confirm key rotation policy (due 2026-01-29).
- [Liam O'Neill] Provision canary network path and confirm traffic shaping (due 2026-02-05).
- [Elena Sorensen / Harbor] Confirm pinned prompts official product wording (due 2026-02-10).

Appendix: sample acceptance record (redacted)
- input_text: "Container 8843 delayed at port; ETA now 2026-01-17; contact John D. (redacted)"
- expected_summary: "Container 8843 delayed; new ETA 2026-01-17; action: notify operations to reassign unloading slot."
- expected_extractions: {origin: "Port of LA", ETA: "2026-01-17", exceptions: "delay at customs"}

Notes & provenance:
- This slate was created after the SOW kick-off call on 2026-01-12 and incorporates Harbor's security checklist. Iterations and comments are tracked in the linked GitHub PR and CONFLUENCE-HAR-4521.
- If pinned prompts need updates post-launch, changes must go through the same acceptance and sign-off flow; emergency patching requires joint written consent from Customer Success and Security.

Document history:
